messages:
sofia (support): FYI incoming customer escalation from ACME — multiple 502/504s on hosted inference around 09:12 UTC. They've attached request IDs and a short trace. Ticket INC-3421. Can ops take a look?
ops-bot: ALERT: gateway-5xx-rate spike (svc=inference-gateway, rate=22/min) at 2026-03-15T09:12:18Z — paging oncall
maya (oncall): looking. initial check: ingress gateway spiked with upstream timeouts to inference-proxy, lots of queued requests. No obvious DB issues. Pasting tail of gateway logs: 
```
[09:12:15Z] 502 upstream timeout to inference-proxy:10.4.3.12:8080 req_id=abc123
[09:12:16Z] 504 request timed out after 30s req_id=abc124
[09:12:20Z] 502 upstream closed before response req_id=abc125
```
sofia (support): customer says errors only happen during bursty traffic (cron jobs + interactive usage) — intermittent, ~10-20% of requests in spike windows. They repro with a 50rps short burst.
raj (sre): can we see autoscaler state around spike? k8s HPA + KEDA are in the stack, right?
maya (oncall): yes. grabbed a few outputs while issue was ongoing: 
```
# kubectl get hpa -n hosted
NAME                REFERENCE              TARGETS   MINPODS   MAXPODS   REPLICAS
model-handler       Deployment/model-hdlr    450%/80%    0         20        0

# kubectl get scaledobject -n hosted model-handler-scaledobject -o yaml
triggers:
  - type: redis
    metadata:
      listName: inference-queue
      queueLength: "100"
cooldownPeriod: 300
minReplicaCount: 0
```
maya (oncall): notable: minReplicaCount is 0 and cooldownPeriod is 300s. During the burst the queue jumped, KEDA started to scale but cooldown + poll interval meant we were still at 0 for first 20–30s. Also containers take ~25s to init the model so even after pod scheduling there was additional warmup -> requests timed out.
luca (runtime): adding that model-init logs show heavy KV cache prefill and a 23s model weight load: 
```
[init] loading weights shard 1/4 ... 16s
[init] kv-cache warmup ... 6s
[init] model ready in 23.1s
```
raj (sre): OK root cause summary: KEDA config allows minReplicaCount 0 + long cooldown/polling -> slow reaction to sudden bursts. Combined with long container/model warmup -> gateway timeout (30s). Also we saw HPA target miscalculation because custom metrics reported spikes only after queue grew.
sofia (support): customer asked if auth/billing could be related — they saw some 401s earlier. Is that separate?
maya (oncall): looked at auth logs: the 401s were transient due to rotated API keys on their side ~09:05 and unrelated. The 5xxs align with scale-up windows at ~09:12. Not billing.
luca (runtime): mitigation options: 
- set KEDA minReplicaCount to 2 for this model (pre-warm).
- reduce KEDA cooldownPeriod to 30s and pollInterval to 5s.
- set HPA minReplicas=2 to ensure k8s doesn't scale to zero.
- add a lightweight fast-start variant model (quantized) as fallback route for initial requests.
- reduce gateway upstream timeout temporarily to 35s? (we hit 30s now) better we increase timeout while rolling the above fixes.
raj (sre): propose an immediate hotfix + longer-term: hotfix = patch ScaledObject and HPA min replicas, also temporarily increase gateway timeout to 45s to avoid user visible 504s during roll. Long term = pre-warm pool + tuning autoscaler triggers and implement health-check + readiness gating so pod is counted as ready only after model init completes.
sofia (support): customer update: they want ETA and workaround. Can we offer a short-lived change?
maya (oncall): will apply hotfix now (patching to minReplicaCount=2 and cooldownPeriod=30). Will also scale deployment to 2 immediately while KEDA ramps. Patching commands: 
```
kubectl patch scaledobject model-handler-scaledobject -n hosted --type='merge' -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":2,"cooldownPeriod":30}}'
kubectl patch hpa model-handler -n hosted -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":2}}'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-hdlr -n hosted
```
maya (oncall): applying patches...
ops-bot: runbook check: change is allowed at S2 severity with postmortem required.
maya (oncall): patched. scaledobject shows minReplicaCount=2, cooldownPeriod=30 now. Rolling restart triggered.
luca (runtime): also applied temporary gateway upstream timeout increase to 45s on the edge config: `timeout upstream 45s` (will revert after validation).
raj (sre): running quick burst test to reproduce: `wrk -t4 -c200 -d30s http://gateway.example.com/v1/generate`
raj (sre): after patches, observed no 502/504s in the 30s burst, average p50 latency 220ms, some requests saw cold-init tail at ~1.2s extra but within gateway timeout.
sofia (support): passing to customer: hotfix applied, recommend they retry now. Notified them we'll follow up with a formal RCA and a permanent mitigation (minReplicas for critical models, pre-warm pool, fallback model route).
maya (oncall): postmortem owners: raj (lead), luca (runtime) — goals: 1) tune KEDA/HPA defaults for hosted tier, 2) implement pre-warm controller for heavy models, 3) add rollout to change default minReplicaCount for model-handler catalog entries. Target dry-run fixes in 72h.
dev-tools-bot: created internal ticket INFOPS-712 with runbook link and required telemetry (queue_depth, pod_ready_delay, init_time_hist).
sofia (support): customer replied: saw recovery, thanks. Will monitor and reopen if they see more 5xxs.
raj (sre): follow-ups: add alert for "pod-ready-delay > 15s" and a KEDA misconfiguration detector (minReplicaCount == 0 + cooldown > 120s) for hosted. I'll file PRs today.
maya (oncall): closing incident channel — leaving notes for postmortem. If anyone needs to audit commands: `kubectl describe scaledobject model-handler-scaledobject -n hosted` and check `kubectl get hpa -n hosted`
sofia (support): thanks team :thumbsup:
